messages:
maria: Heads-up: rolling firmware push to edge racks in us-west-2 started at ~08:12 PT. Observing ~12% of GPU nodes fail to rejoin OOB after BMC rewrite. Some hosts show secure-boot toggled to 'enabled' unexpectedly. tagging @sre-oncall
kevin: Ack. Which build tag? Is this the microcode+bios package from yesterday?
maria: It's fw-v3.4.1+uefi-opts. We pushed to a 10% canary earlier and looked clean. This roll started auto-stagger for the remaining racks ~08:10.
sre-oncall: I'm on it. Can you paste the failing host IDs and last ipmitool output?
maria: host ids: edge-usw2-rack12-node[04,09,11,13,21]
maria: Sample: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.1.12.09 -U redwood -P **** chassis bootparam get 5` -> returns BootFlag: UEFI:Enabled
kevin: That's the problem — we expected BootFlag: UEFI:Disabled for our provisioning flow. Secure-boot flip causes the PXE chain to drop and node never hits the provisioner.
jamal: Seen similar when NVRAM preserved across flash. Did the update change the efivars write behavior?
maria: fw vendor notes say "preserve-efivars=true" by default unless --reset-vars passed. We didn't pass it.
levi: Ops: If nodes are stuck in UEFI, they won't accept our initramfs netboot. We have a waitlist: ~42 GPU pods blocked in us-west-2. That equates to ~340 GPU-hours backlog and rising.
sre-oncall: Rollout paused. @deploy-bot can you halt the firmware pipeline?
deploy-bot: pipeline fw-rollout/us-west-2 paused by request of @sre-oncall at 08:26 PT :white_flag:
maria: Thanks. For the already-updated nodes, can we do a remediation? Possible options: 1) remote efivar reset via ipmi SOL, 2) schedule local techs for kvm/serial interaction, 3) rollback image to previous version that had reset-vars.\evi: (typo) — levi: option (1) looks feasible for many but SOL sessions are thin and serial bandwidth is limited. Doing it at scale will cause OOB queueing.
kevin: Also network-wise the remote-serial gateway to that site has 120ms median queue now; pushing more SOL sessions will saturate and risk other control-plane tasks.
jamal: Quick hack: can we set a temporary policy in the provisioner to accept UEFI:Enabled nodes by using an alternate boot script? Might let them PXE into a shim that toggles secure boot off in-ram and continue.
sre-oncall: That could work for some models but risky. Need a tested fallback. We can't flip unsigned kernel chain policy quickly.
maria: I've got a small script that checks efivar and if UEFI:Enabled tries `efibootmgr --delete-bootnum` and `efivar --set -n BootCurrent` but would require mounting an initramfs image with efivars exposed.
kevin: If we go that route, we need a canary of 3 nodes first and alert the security team.
jamal: Cost note: every hour of backlog is ~ $420 in delayed job costs + $80 in on-call burn if we do manual SOL. If rollback to fw-v3.4.0, estimate restart time per node ~9 minutes, which might be faster but risks other regressions.
levi: Region constraint: us-west-2 has limited spare capacity; moving workloads to other regions will add egress and cross-region infra costs and PCI considerations for some customers. Not ideal.
sre-oncall: Decision tree? A) attempt remote efivar reset via scripted initramfs + canary 3 nodes (low infra cost, moderate risk) B) rollback firmware for the rest (higher risk of repeating whatever prompted fw bump) C) manual SOL for stuck nodes (safe but expensive & slow).
maria: I'm inclined A + B contingency. I'll prepare the initramfs and a low-risk bootstrap that only toggles efivars and exits.
kevin: I'll draft a short runbook for the initramfs path and include automated abort on unusual efivar states. Jamal, can you run cost calc for A vs C for the next 24h?
jamal: On it. Preliminary: A projected ~ $900 ops + small infra churn; C projected ~ $4200 ops + 24-48h backlog.
sre-oncall: Ok proceed with canary A. Block further rollouts until canary green and security sign-off. Notify CS for potential customer impact.
deploy-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-033 — edge-fw-uefi-flip-usw2. Pipeline wf paused.
maria: Canary repro steps pushed to /runbooks/edge-uefi-remediate (private). Will update here after canary results.
kevin: Thx. Keep replies short in this thread — we need to coordinate the hands-on steps.
sre-oncall: Monitoring: watch provisioner queue length, OOB gateway latency, and failed boot events. I'll set alerts for queue > 20 and SOL latency > 200ms.
maria: Canary started at 08:44 PT. 3 nodes, serial logs attached to the runbook.
kevin: Canary is green at 08:58 PT — efivar reset successful on all three, nodes reprovisioned.
jamal: Recomputed costs: A wins for near-term. Recommend scripted remediation for the remaining 9 affected racks.
sre-oncall: Good. Proceed with staged remediation, 2 racks at a time to avoid gateway saturation. Keep CS updated.
maria: Will post incremental status every batch. Thanks team.
